governance_summary.framework_attribution: IPCC AR6 Working Group II Conceptual Framework (Risk = f(H, E, V)) vs CLIMORA Multiplicative Power-Law Implementation (Risk = H^alpha * E^beta * V^gamma)
governance_summary.spatial_autocorrelation_caveat: Spatial pixels are not i.i.d. (Moran's I > 0); standard error sigma / sqrt(n) is mathematically disqualified
governance_summary.susceptibility_semantics_boundary: Susceptibility is strictly Biophysical and Structural (1 - NDVI, NDBI). Satellite spectral indices do NOT measure socioeconomic poverty or income
governance_summary.threshold_qualification: 45.0C is a CLIMORA methodological surface temperature screening threshold, not an epidemiological or WHO heat-health threshold
governance_summary.temporal_missing_data_rule: Cell eligibility requires valid pixel coverage >= 0.70; baseline statistics require K_valid >= 4 of 5 years
governance_summary.active_mesh: Uber H3 Discrete Global Grid System Resolution 9 (3,181 cells in statutory Pune AOI)

formulation_groups: 5. Multi-Temporal Microclimatic Baseline & Dynamic Heat Metrics
7. Composite Hazard, Exposure, and Susceptibility Components

formulations.name: Landsat 8/9 OLI Surface Reflectance

variable_definitions.DN_lambda: 16-bit unsigned integer digital number for band lambda

formulations.scientific_purpose: Atmospheric correction of top-of-atmosphere radiance to surface reflectance
assumptions: USGS LaSRC code reliably models aerosol optical depth and ozone absorption
limitations: Residual adjacency and topographic shadow effects on hillslopes
formulations.validation_method: USGS cross-calibration against MODIS and Sentinel-2 (+/- 2% radiometric accuracy)
formulations.provenance_source: USGS Landsat Collection 2 Level 2 Science Product Guide

formulations.name: Landsat 8/9 TIRS Surface Temperature

variable_definitions.DN_ST_B10: 16-bit unsigned integer digital number from ST_B10
variable_definitions.T_C: Land surface temperature in degrees Celsius (T_K - 273.15)

formulations.scientific_purpose: Retrieval of surface radiometric skin temperature during mid-morning overpass (~10:30 AM local time)
assumptions: ASTER GED emissivity and MERRA-2 atmospheric profiles provide accurate single-channel inversion
limitations: Measures surface skin temperature, not ambient 2m air temperature; morning overpass precedes peak afternoon diurnal heating
formulations.validation_method: USGS ground pyrometer validation indicating RMSE of +/- 1.0 K to +/- 1.5 K under clear-sky conditions
formulations.provenance_source: Cook et al. (2014); Malakar et al. (2018); USGS C2 L2 ST Documentation

formulations.name: Quality Assessment Pixel Masking
formulations.expression_ascii: M_valid = (QA_PIXEL bit 1==0 and bit 3==0 and bit 4==0 and bit 6==1) and (QA_RADSAT == 0)

variable_definitions.QA_PIXEL: CFMask 16-bit bitmask of cloud, dilated cloud, shadow, and clear surface
variable_definitions.M_valid: Binary clear terrestrial pixel validity flag (1 = valid, 0 = masked)

formulations.scientific_purpose: Filter out cloud, cloud shadow, and saturated pixels prior to calculating biophysical indices or zonal statistics
assumptions: CFMask reliably detects tropical clouds and shadow over dry urban surfaces
limitations: Thin cirrus or sub-pixel plumes may evade detection
formulations.validation_method: Visual inspection of true-color RGB composites against QA mask raster

formulations.name: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index

variable_definitions.NIR: Surface reflectance in Near-Infrared (Band 5 Landsat 8/9, Band 8 Sentinel-2)
variable_definitions.Red: Surface reflectance in Red (Band 4 Landsat 8/9 and Sentinel-2)

formulations.scientific_purpose: Proxy for photosynthetic canopy cover capable of evaporative cooling
assumptions: Chlorophyll absorption in red and cellular scattering in NIR correlates with live vegetative biomass
limitations: Saturates in high biomass; subject to pre-monsoon deciduous leaf senescence; DOES NOT measure human poverty or income
formulations.validation_method: Rouse et al. (1974); cross-sensor consistency with Sentinel-2 10m NDVI (R2 > 0.92)

formulations.name: Normalized Difference Built-up Index

variable_definitions.SWIR1: Surface reflectance in SWIR1 (Band 6 Landsat 8/9, Band 11 Sentinel-2)
variable_definitions.NIR: Surface reflectance in Near-Infrared (Band 5 Landsat 8/9, Band 8 Sentinel-2)

formulations.scientific_purpose: Proxy for impervious built surfaces, masonry, concrete, tin, and asphalt thermal mass
assumptions: Built materials exhibit higher SWIR reflectance than NIR reflectance
limitations: Bare dry soil and rocky basalt outcrops also yield positive NDBI; DOES NOT measure socioeconomic deprivation
formulations.validation_method: Zha et al. (2003); cross-validation against OSM building and road vectors

formulations.name: Normalized Difference Water Index Policy
formulations.scientific_purpose: Delineation of open water bodies and surface moisture
assumptions: Water absorbs strongly in NIR while reflecting moderately in green
limitations: NOT currently generated in data lake; excluded from active feature dictionary to preserve lineage integrity
formulations.validation_method: OpenStreetMap vector water bodies currently utilized instead (feat_water_body_area_m2)
formulations.provenance_source: McFeeters (1996); Phase 1B Forensic Amendment Gate Section 11

formulations.name: H3 Cell Valid Pixel Coverage Fraction

variable_definitions.P_i: Set of raster pixel centroids intersecting H3 cell i
variable_definitions.M_valid: Binary pixel validity mask (1 = clear, 0 = cloud/masked)
variable_definitions.f_valid: Fraction of cell area with valid clear pixels in year t

formulations.scientific_purpose: Ensure spatial statistical sample within H3 hexagon is representative before computing zonal features
assumptions: A cell with >= 70% unmasked pixels provides an unbiased estimate of cell microclimate
limitations: Cells with < 70% valid coverage are rejected and flagged INVALID_ANNUAL_COVERAGE
formulations.validation_method: Automated unit tests in test_phase_1b_analytical_contracts.py

formulations.name: Continuous Raster Zonal Mean, Median, and Percentiles
formulations.expression_latex: \bar{x}_{i, t} = \frac{1}{N_{\text{valid}, i, t}} \sum_{p=1}^{N_{\text{valid}, i, t}} x_{p, t}
formulations.expression_ascii: x_bar = mean(x_p for p in valid_pixels_in_cell_i)

variable_definitions.x_p: Continuous pixel value (LST, NDVI, NDBI, Elevation, Slope)
variable_definitions.N_valid: Count of clear unmasked pixels in cell i
variable_definitions.P75, P90: 75th and 90th empirical percentiles within the cell

formulations.scientific_purpose: Summarize high-resolution pixel values into the canonical H3 Res 9 modeling mesh
assumptions: Pixel order statistics accurately represent sub-hex distribution
limitations: Within-hex spatial gradients are collapsed into summary statistics
formulations.validation_method: Zonal extraction verification against exact raster arrays in test_phase_1a8_processing.py

formulations.name: Zonal Sample Standard Deviation and Autocorrelation Caveat

variable_definitions.s_i: Sample standard deviation of within-cell pixel values

formulations.scientific_purpose: Measure within-cell sub-grid spatial heterogeneity
assumptions: Sub-grid variance reflects mixed land-cover (e.g. tree canopy interspersed with asphalt)
limitations: STRICT BAN on reporting s / sqrt(N) as standard error; adjacent pixels have Moran's I > 0 and are not i.i.d.
formulations.validation_method: Sample variance tests in test_phase_1b_analytical_contracts.py

formulations.name: Area-Weighted Dasymetric Population Sum
formulations.expression_ascii: C_i = sum(C_P * Area(h_i intersect P) / Area(P))

variable_definitions.C_i: Estimated resident population count in H3 cell h_i
variable_definitions.C_P: Estimated population in WorldPop 1km grid pixel P
variable_definitions.Area(h_i intersect P): Metric intersection area evaluated in EPSG:32643
variable_definitions.Area(P): Total area of 1km raster pixel P

formulations.scientific_purpose: Spatially disaggregate 1km regional population counts into 9.86 ha H3 hexagons while rigorously conserving mass
assumptions: Demographic density is uniform within each 1km dasymetric pixel
limitations: Captures residential night population; does not model daytime commercial commuter surges
formulations.validation_method: Conservation audit against exact polygon clip (5,011,396.9 exact vs 5,011,229.6 aggregated; delta 0.0033% <= 0.05% tolerance)
formulations.provenance_source: Stevens et al. (2015); CLIMORA Population Exposure Contract

formulations.name: Population Density

variable_definitions.D_i: Population density in persons per square kilometer
variable_definitions.A_i: Actual geodesic area of cell i in km2 (via h3.cell_area(c, unit='km^2'))

input_data: A_i from geodesic H3 cell geometry
formulations.scientific_purpose: Quantify spatial intensity of human exposure to heat hazard
assumptions: Population is distributed across the hexagon's geodesic area
limitations: Represents spatial intensity, not social vulnerability or adaptive capacity
formulations.validation_method: Automated ratio checks against cell geodesic area in test_phase_1c_feature_matrix.py
formulations.provenance_source: CLIMORA Population Exposure Contract (Phase 1C.1 Geodesic Amendment)

formulations.name: Multi-Type Infrastructure Asset Exposure
formulations.expression_latex: N_{\text{infra}, i} = \sum_{k} \mathbb{I}(p_k \in h_i), \quad L_{\text{road}, i} = \sum_{s} \text{Length}_{\text{EPSG:32643}}(s \cap h_i)

variable_definitions.N_infra: Integer count of hospitals, clinics, schools, universities in cell i
variable_definitions.L_road: Total length of road centerline segments within cell i in meters
variable_definitions.A_green, A_water: Total area of parks/greenery and water bodies within cell i in square meters

formulations.scientific_purpose: Quantify physical infrastructure assets and environmental buffers exposed to thermal stress
assumptions: OSM geometries accurately reflect current municipal physical infrastructure in Pune
limitations: OSM crowdsourced data may exhibit spatial completeness variation between central and fringe wards
formulations.validation_method: Planar geometric verification in EPSG:32643 UTM Zone 43N
formulations.provenance_source: OpenStreetMap contributors; CLIMORA Spatial Harmonization Engine

formulations.name: Annual Valid Observation Count
formulations.group: 5. Multi-Temporal Microclimatic Baseline & Dynamic Heat Metrics

variable_definitions.K_valid_i: Number of baseline years satisfying valid pixel coverage criterion (0 to 5)

formulations.scientific_purpose: Govern baseline eligibility: cells with K_valid < 4 are disqualified from baseline central tendencies
assumptions: A minimum of 4 annual observations is necessary to bound interannual pre-monsoon variability
limitations: Cells with K_valid < 4 are flagged INSUFFICIENT_HISTORICAL_COVERAGE
formulations.validation_method: Temporal governance audit tests in test_temporal_governance.py

formulations.name: 5-Year Baseline LST Mean and Standard Deviation
formulations.group: 5. Multi-Temporal Microclimatic Baseline & Dynamic Heat Metrics
formulations.expression_latex: \bar{T}_{\text{base}, i} = \frac{1}{K_{\text{valid}, i}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{V}_i} \bar{T}_{i, t}, \quad \sigma_{\text{base}, i} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{K_i - 1} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{V}_i} (\bar{T}_{i, t} - \bar{T}_{\text{base}, i})^2}
formulations.expression_ascii: T_base_mean = mean(T_i_t for t in valid_years); sigma_base = std(T_i_t for t in valid_years)

variable_definitions.T_base_mean: 5-year baseline arithmetic mean of pre-monsoon morning LST
variable_definitions.sigma_base: Temporal interannual standard deviation across valid years

formulations.scientific_purpose: Establish stable 5-year pre-monsoon microclimatic reference baseline (2021-2025)
assumptions: Five April scenes capture pre-monsoon peak heating; does not represent a 30-year WMO climate trend
limitations: Requires K_valid >= 4; evaluated strictly across approved April baseline scenes
formulations.validation_method: Multi-temporal stack verification in test_phase_1a8_processing.py

formulations.name: 2025 Current-State Thermal Anomaly
formulations.group: 5. Multi-Temporal Microclimatic Baseline & Dynamic Heat Metrics
formulations.expression_latex: \Delta T_{2025, i} = \bar{T}_{2025, i} - \bar{T}_{\text{base}, i}, \quad z_{2025, i} = \frac{\bar{T}_{2025, i} - \bar{T}_{\text{base}, i}}{\sigma_{\text{base}, i} + \varepsilon}

variable_definitions.Delta_T: Absolute thermal anomaly in degrees Celsius
variable_definitions.epsilon: NUMERICAL_STABILITY_PARAMETER (0.001 C) defensive safeguard preventing division by zero

formulations.units: Delta_T in celsius; z is dimensionless
formulations.scientific_purpose: Isolate acute localized statistical departures from the multi-annual microclimatic baseline
assumptions: Interannual baseline provides a robust expectation of normal pre-monsoon temperature
limitations: Valid iff cell has K_valid >= 4 and f_valid_2025 >= 0.70; z-score is a statistical screening metric, not a validated physiological indicator; epsilon exists as a defensive numerical safeguard but was not activated for any eligible cell
formulations.validation_method: Mathematical edge case verification in test_phase_1c_feature_matrix.py

formulations.name: Heat Persistence (Top Quartile Frequency)
formulations.group: 5. Multi-Temporal Microclimatic Baseline & Dynamic Heat Metrics
formulations.expression_ascii: Persistence_i = sum(I(T_i_t >= P75_citywide_t) for t in valid_years) / K_valid_i

variable_definitions.P75_t: City-wide 75th percentile of valid cell mean LST in year t
variable_definitions.Persistence_i: Proportion of valid baseline years where cell was in the city's top 25% hottest areas

input_data: Annual cell mean LST for 2021 to 2025
formulations.scientific_purpose: Identify structurally chronic urban heat island cores that persist across multiple years
assumptions: A cell repeatedly falling into the top quartile represents chronic built-environment heat retention
limitations: Measures RELATIVE surface temperature persistence within the city; NOT human heat-health strain
formulations.validation_method: Consistency checks in test_phase_1b_analytical_contracts.py

formulations.name: Extreme LST Recurrence (>= 45C Threshold)
formulations.group: 5. Multi-Temporal Microclimatic Baseline & Dynamic Heat Metrics
formulations.expression_ascii: Recurrence_45_i = sum(I(T_i_t >= 45.0C) for t in valid_years)

variable_definitions.Recurrence_45_i: Integer count of valid baseline annual observations where cell mean LST >= 45.0 C

input_data: Annual cell mean LST for 2021 to 2025
formulations.scientific_purpose: Identify zones subject to acute physical surface heating on impervious materials
assumptions: 45.0C is a meaningful screening threshold for severe radiant heat on tin roofs and asphalt
limitations: CLIMORA Methodological Threshold; strictly NOT an epidemiological, clinical, or WHO threshold
formulations.validation_method: Contract compliance tests in test_phase_1b_analytical_contracts.py

formulations.name: Linear and Robust Quantile Normalization
formulations.expression_latex: x'_i = \frac{x_i - x_{\min}}{x_{\max} - x_{\min}} \quad \text{or} \quad x'_i = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{x_i - P_2(x)}{P_{98}(x) - P_2(x)}, 0.0, 1.0\right)
formulations.expression_ascii: Norm_minmax = (x - min) / (max - min); Norm_robust = clamp((x - P2) / (P98 - P2), 0, 1)

variable_definitions.x_i: Raw feature value in cell i

formulations.scientific_purpose: Transform heterogeneous physical variables into uniform dimensionless scales for index aggregation
assumptions: Min-max or Winsorized scaling preserves relative ranking and variance
limitations: Linear min-max is sensitive to extreme single-pixel outliers; robust Winsorization mitigates outlier leverage
formulations.validation_method: Distribution boundary checks in test_phase_1b_analytical_contracts.py

formulations.name: Composite Thermal Hazard Index
formulations.group: 7. Composite Hazard, Exposure, and Susceptibility Components
formulations.expression_latex: \mathcal{H}_i = w_{H, 1} \text{Norm}(\bar{T}_{2025, i}) + w_{H, 2} \text{Norm}(\Delta T_{2025, i}) + w_{H, 3} \text{Persistence}_i + w_{H, 4} \text{Norm}(\text{Recurrence}_{45, i})
formulations.expression_ascii: H_i = w_H1 * Norm(T_2025) + w_H2 * Norm(Delta_T) + w_H3 * Persistence + w_H4 * Norm(Recurrence_45)
formulations.scientific_purpose: Synthesize current intensity, acute departure, chronic persistence, and extreme thermal threshold crossings
assumptions: Equal weighting is a CLIMORA_INITIAL_METHODOLOGICAL_ASSUMPTION (PENDING_CALIBRATION)
limitations: Linear additive combination within hazard requires sensitivity testing
formulations.validation_method: Multi-attribute sensitivity analysis across [0.1, 0.5] weight envelopes

formulations.name: Composite Human and Asset Exposure Index
formulations.group: 7. Composite Hazard, Exposure, and Susceptibility Components

variable_definitions.E_i: Composite human and critical infrastructure exposure index in [0.0, 1.0]

formulations.scientific_purpose: Measure presence and spatial intensity of humans and critical assets exposed to heat hazard
assumptions: Population and critical infrastructure represent primary exposure assets
limitations: Weights are methodological assumptions; zero exposure strictly yields E_i = 0
formulations.validation_method: Zero-exposure boundary verification tests

formulations.name: Biophysical and Structural Susceptibility Index
formulations.group: 7. Composite Hazard, Exposure, and Susceptibility Components

variable_definitions.V_i: Biophysical and structural susceptibility score in [0.0, 1.0]

formulations.scientific_purpose: Quantify physical surface properties that amplify radiant heat stress
assumptions: Lack of tree canopy and presence of dense built materials exacerbate surface heating
limitations: STRICT BOUNDARY: Does NOT measure human poverty, household income, or adaptive capacity
formulations.validation_method: Correlation analysis against ground-measured surface temperatures

formulations.name: Multiplicative Power-Law Climate Risk Model

variable_definitions.Risk_i: Composite climate risk score bounded in [0.0, 1.0]

formulations.scientific_purpose: Operationalize IPCC AR6 risk framework while mathematically enforcing the zero-exposure axiom
assumptions: Zero exposure implies zero human risk (E_i = 0 => Risk_i = 0)
limitations: Power-law form is a CLIMORA methodological implementation, NOT an IPCC-prescribed formula
formulations.validation_method: Automated zero-exposure boundary and numerical stability testing

formulations.name: Global and Local Moran's I Hotspot Detection
formulations.expression_ascii: Global Moran's I and Local Moran's I (LISA) on H3 6-neighbor adjacency

variable_definitions.I: Global Moran's I spatial autocorrelation coefficient
variable_definitions.I_i: Local Moran's I statistic for cell i

formulations.units: I is dimensionless in [-1.0, 1.0]; I_i is dimensionless
input_data: Risk_i or LST_i across 3,181 H3 cells
output_data: hotspot_classification: High-High, Low-Low, High-Low, Low-High, Not-Significant
formulations.scientific_purpose: Differentiate isolated extreme cells from statistically significant spatial clusters (urban heat island hotspots)
assumptions: 6-neighbor isotropic adjacency accurately models spatial heat diffusion
limitations: Requires multi-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR) to control false positives
formulations.validation_method: Permutation testing (999 Monte Carlo iterations) and analytical variance testing

formulations.name: Spatial Intervention Allocation Model (MILP)
formulations.expression_latex: \max \Phi = \lambda_1 \sum_i C_i \sum_j \Delta T_{j} x_{j, i} + \lambda_2 \sum_i \text{Infra}_i \sum_j \Delta T_j x_{j, i} - \lambda_3 \text{Gini}(\text{Benefit})
formulations.expression_ascii: max Objective subject to sum(Cost_j * x_j_i) <= Budget and x_j_i <= MaxEligible_j_i

variable_definitions.x_j_i: Decision variable: allocation fraction of cooling intervention j in cell i
variable_definitions.Delta_T_j: Expected microclimatic cooling effect of intervention j

formulations.scientific_purpose: Optimize spatial deployment of cool roofs, urban tree canopy, and misting shelters under budgetary constraints
assumptions: Cool roof eligibility bounded by impervious roof fraction heuristic (f_roof_potential = 0.60)
limitations: Optimization depends on assumed unit costs and scenario cooling coefficients
formulations.validation_method: Linear programming solver validation (PuLP / SciPy linprog)

formulations.name: Modeled Cooling Impact and Population-Weighted Benefit
formulations.expression_latex: T_{\text{post}, i} = \bar{T}_{\text{base}, i} - \sum_j \Delta T_j x_{j, i}, \quad \text{PWBenefit} = \frac{\sum_i C_i (\bar{T}_{\text{base}, i} - T_{\text{post}, i})}{\sum_i C_i}
formulations.expression_ascii: T_post = T_base - sum(Delta_T_j * x_j_i); PWBenefit = sum(C_i * Benefit_i) / sum(C_i)

variable_definitions.T_post: Modeled post-intervention surface temperature in Celsius
variable_definitions.Benefit_i: Modeled temperature reduction in cell i
variable_definitions.PWBenefit: Population-weighted cooling benefit across the city

formulations.scientific_purpose: Quantify projected thermal relief and human exposure reduction achieved by proposed interventions
assumptions: Thermodynamic boundary: T_post cannot drop below ambient wet-bulb equilibrium
limitations: Cooling effects are SCENARIO ASSUMPTIONS, never presented as measured real-world observations
formulations.validation_method: Thermodynamic bounding checks against NASA POWER wet-bulb temperatures

formulations.name: Difference-in-Differences Causal Verification

variable_definitions.tau_DID: Causal average treatment effect on the treated (ATT)
variable_definitions.Y_treat: Observed LST in treated intervention cells
variable_definitions.Y_control: Observed LST in matched untreated control cells

input_data: Pre- and post-intervention satellite observations across treated and control cells
formulations.scientific_purpose: Rigorously isolate intervention cooling effect from synoptic weather variations and regional climate trends
assumptions: Parallel trends assumption holds between treated and matched control hexagons
limitations: Requires future physical implementation and multi-year post-intervention satellite acquisitions
formulations.validation_method: Placebo tests, pre-intervention trend validation, and propensity score matching
formulations.provenance_source: Angrist and Pischke (2009); CLIMORA Analytical Architecture

formulations.name: Component-Wise Uncertainty Propagation

variable_definitions.sigma_sensor: Instrument radiometric uncertainty (+/- 1.0 to 1.5 K; DOCUMENTED_EXTERNAL)

input_data: Zonal stats, sensor specs, demographic specs
formulations.scientific_purpose: Disaggregate and propagate uncertainty transparently across all analytical stages
assumptions: Quadrature sum valid only where components are mutually uncorrelated
limitations: Component-wise uncertainty reporting is mandatory where spatial autocorrelation exists
formulations.validation_method: Monte Carlo error propagation simulations

formulations.name: Global and Local Sensitivity Analysis
formulations.expression_latex: S_p = \frac{\partial \ln \text{Risk}_i}{\partial \ln p} = p \ln X_i, \quad S_k = \frac{\text{Var}_{p_k}(E_{p_{\sim k}}[\text{Risk} \mid p_k])}{\text{Var}(\text{Risk})}
formulations.expression_ascii: S_alpha = alpha * ln(H_i); S_beta = beta * ln(E_i); S_gamma = gamma * ln(V_i)

variable_definitions.S_p: Local elasticity of Risk with respect to parameter p in {alpha, beta, gamma}

formulations.scientific_purpose: Quantify sensitivity of risk rankings and hotspot boundaries to variations in alpha, beta, gamma, and weights
assumptions: Uniform parameter exploration over [0.5, 2.0] covers plausible decision space
limitations: Evaluates model structural stability; does not validate physical ground truth
formulations.validation_method: Sobol variance decomposition and Morris screening method
formulations.provenance_source: Saltelli et al. (2008); CLIMORA Analytical Architecture
